a: The DOM is the browser's tree representation of an HTML page that JavaScript can read and update.
A Single Page Application loads one page and updates the UI with JavaScript without full reloads.
Server-Side Rendering builds HTML on the server for faster first paint and better SEO.
Client-Side Rendering builds the UI in the browser with JavaScript after loading a shell page.
A React component is a reusable UI piece that returns JSX.
Props are inputs passed from a parent component to a child.
State is data a component owns and can update, causing a re-render.
The key prop helps React identify list items when reconciling updates.
React Router maps URLs to components for navigation in a React app.
Next.js is a React framework with routing, SSR/SSG, and API routes.
Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework for building designs with class names.
Accessibility (a11y) means designing UIs so people with disabilities can use them (keyboard, screen readers, contrast).
Responsive design makes layouts adapt to phone, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.
A Progressive Web App can be installed, work offline, and feel more like a native app.
A JS bundle is the packaged frontend code shipped to the browser (often via webpack/vite).
Vite is a fast frontend build tool and dev server popular with React and Vue.
Webpack bundles JavaScript modules and assets for the browser.
A CORS preflight is an OPTIONS request the browser sends before some cross-origin requests.
